question: Can a cross-validation-tuned model (LightGBM / SVM / ExtraTrees soft-voting ensemble with engineered pairwise-difference features) beat a standard MLP at indoor location classification from signal-strength readings?
method: One stratified 80/20 split (seed 42), shared standardisation fit on train. Baseline: sklearn MLPClassifier. Improved: LightGBM (on raw + pairwise-difference features) and RBF-SVM tuned by 5-fold CV on the training set only, combined with ExtraTrees in a soft-voting ensemble; the final improved model (ensemble vs. single components) is chosen by training-set CV accuracy. Test set used once; randomized models run with seeds 42, 43, 44 (means reported).
baseline: scikit-learn MLPClassifier, one hidden layer of 100 ReLU units, Adam, max_iter=500 (stand-in for the paper's deep model).
improved: Selected by CV: ensemble. Candidates: soft-voting ensemble of CV-tuned LightGBM + CV-tuned RBF-SVC + ExtraTrees (300 trees), tree models use added pairwise signal-difference features.
notes: Stand-in dataset, not the paper's RFID data; the paper's model (EDEEPRFID-IPS) is not reproduced. Selected improved model: ensemble; LightGBM params {'learning_rate': 0.05, 'n_estimators': 100, 'num_leaves': 4}; SVC params {'C': 3, 'gamma': 0.3}. Training-set CV accuracy: {'ensemble': 0.9856250000000001, 'svc': 0.9831249999999999, 'lightgbm': 0.985625}. Hyper-parameters and model choice tuned once with seed 42 using CV on the training set only; seeds only change final fits. The baseline MLP, split, scaler and evaluation code are unchanged. Timing is wall-clock on the CI CPU; the ensemble is slower per prediction than a small LightGBM, and timings are noisy and are not measurements on a real small device. Accuracy differences may be within seed/split noise (single split).
